source: Mixed: PITAHC Herbs Directory, WHO IMCI Chart Booklet, Saunders Q&A Review 7th ed., Brunner & Suddarth 16e Test Bank (Ch. 1)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Community Health Nursing Process & Primary Health Care
questions.stem: A mother asks the barangay health nurse for a herbal remedy for her child's cough. Which DOH-approved herbal medicine should the nurse recommend?
questions.rationale: Lagundi (Vitex negundo) is the DOH-approved herbal medicine for cough.
explanations: Sambong is for kidney stones and is a diuretic.
Correct: lagundi is used for cough.
Akapulko is for ringworm and other fungal infections.
Niyog-niyogan is for intestinal worms.
questions.source: PITAHC Herbs Directory (pitahc.gov.ph/herbs-directory), Lagundi
questions.quote: For cough

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Community Health Nursing Process & Primary Health Care
questions.stem: A client is using a sambong decoction for kidney stones. Which instruction about fluids should the nurse give?
options: Limit water to 4 glasses a day
Drink the decoction only once a week
Drink 12 or more glasses of water daily
Avoid water for an hour after each dose
questions.rationale: Sambong (Blumea balsamifera) is used for kidney stones. The decoction is divided into 3 portions taken 3 times a day, with 12 or more glasses of water daily.
explanations: Fluids are increased, not restricted.
The decoction is taken 3 times a day.
Correct: high fluid intake is part of the instructions.
There is no such restriction.
questions.source: PITAHC Herbs Directory (pitahc.gov.ph/herbs-directory), Sambong
questions.quote: Drink 12 glasses of water or more daily.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Community Health Nursing Process & Primary Health Care
questions.stem: A mother will use akapulko leaf extract on her son's buni (ringworm). How should the nurse tell her to apply it?
options: Twice a day, every day, for 3 weeks
Once a week for a month
Every hour until the itching stops
questions.rationale: Akapulko (Senna alata) extract is applied to the affected skin twice a day, daily for 3 weeks, to fully kill the fungus.
explanations: Correct: twice daily for 3 weeks.
Too short to kill the fungus.
Too infrequent to work.
Not the recommended frequency.
questions.source: PITAHC Herbs Directory (pitahc.gov.ph/herbs-directory), Akapulko
questions.quote: Apply it daily within 3 weeks to completely kill the fungus that causes ringworm and other fungal infections.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Community Health Nursing Process & Primary Health Care
questions.stem: How many niyog-niyogan seeds should a 9-year-old with intestinal worms chew as a single dose?
questions.rationale: Niyog-niyogan (Quisqualis indica) seeds are dosed by age: 4 to 5 seeds (4 to 6 years), 6 to 7 seeds (7 to 12 years), and 8 to 10 seeds (13 years and above). The dose may be repeated after 1 week if no worms are expelled.
explanations: This is the dose for 4 to 6 years old.
This is the dose for 13 years and above.
This exceeds every recommended dose.
Correct: the dose for 7 to 12 years old.
questions.source: PITAHC Herbs Directory (pitahc.gov.ph/herbs-directory), Niyog-niyogan
questions.quote: 6–7 seeds (7–12 years old)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Community Health Nursing Process & Primary Health Care
questions.stem: A mother plans to give tsaang-gubat tea to her 5-year-old for stomach pain. What is the nurse's BEST response?
options: 'Give 3 tablespoons of leaves boiled in water.'
'Tsaang-gubat is not recommended for children below 7.'
'Give it with milk to protect the stomach.'
'Use lagundi instead; it also relieves stomach pain.'
questions.rationale: Tsaang-gubat (Carmona retusa) is used for stomach pain but is not recommended for children below 7 years old. If the pain persists, the client should consult a doctor.
explanations: Three tablespoons is the dose for 13 years and older.
Correct: it is not recommended under 7 years.
This is not part of the guidance.
Lagundi is for cough, not stomach pain.
questions.source: PITAHC Herbs Directory (pitahc.gov.ph/herbs-directory), Tsaang-gubat
questions.quote: not recommended for children below 7 years old.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Community Health Nursing Process & Primary Health Care
questions.stem: Which DOH-approved herbal medicine is used to help control uric acid levels in gout?
questions.rationale: Ulasimang bato or pansit-pansitan (Peperomia pellucida) helps control uric acid, used under a doctor's advice. Ampalaya is for diabetes, bawang for high cholesterol, and yerba buena for pain.
explanations: Ampalaya helps control blood sugar in diabetes.
Bawang (garlic) is for high blood cholesterol.
Correct: used to help control uric acid.
Yerba buena is an analgesic for toothache and headache.
questions.source: PITAHC Herbs Directory (pitahc.gov.ph/herbs-directory), Ulasimang bato
questions.quote: Tips on how to control uric acid

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Using IMCI, which finding in a sick child aged 2 months to 5 years is a GENERAL DANGER SIGN?
questions.rationale: The general danger signs are: unable to drink or breastfeed, vomits everything, history of convulsions, lethargic or unconscious, and convulsing now.
explanations: Correct: vomiting everything is a general danger sign.
Fever is assessed under its own main symptom.
Cough is assessed under cough or difficult breathing.
A cold is not a danger sign.
questions.source: WHO IMCI Chart Booklet (Afghanistan adaptation), p. 2
questions.quote: Child vomits everything

questions.subject: NP I
questions.situation: At the barangay health station, Nurse Joy assesses 2-year-old Migo, who weighs 12 kg and has had diarrhea for 3 days. He is restless and irritable, has sunken eyes, drinks eagerly, and his skin pinch goes back slowly. There is no blood in the stool and no general danger sign.
questions.stem: How should Nurse Joy classify Migo's dehydration?
questions.rationale: Two or more of these signs mean SOME DEHYDRATION: restless or irritable, sunken eyes, drinks eagerly or thirsty, skin pinch goes back slowly. Severe dehydration needs signs such as lethargy, inability to drink, or a very slow skin pinch.
explanations: Severe dehydration needs lethargy, poor drinking, or a very slow skin pinch.
He has more than enough signs for dehydration.
Persistent diarrhea is 14 days or more.
Correct: he has two or more 'some dehydration' signs.
questions.source: WHO IMCI Chart Booklet (Afghanistan adaptation), p. 3
questions.quote: Child drinks eagerly, thirsty

questions.subject: NP I
questions.situation: At the barangay health station, Nurse Joy assesses 2-year-old Migo, who weighs 12 kg and has had diarrhea for 3 days. He is restless and irritable, has sunken eyes, drinks eagerly, and his skin pinch goes back slowly. There is no blood in the stool and no general danger sign.
questions.stem: Under Plan B, about how much ORS should Migo receive in the clinic over the first 4 hours?
questions.rationale: The approximate ORS amount for the first 4 hours is weight (kg) × 75 mL: 12 × 75 = 900 mL. Give more if the child wants more.
explanations: This is 50 mL/kg, too little.
This is 100 mL/kg, the Plan C amount.
Correct: 12 kg × 75 mL = 900 mL.
This is 150 mL/kg, far too much.
questions.source: WHO IMCI Chart Booklet (Afghanistan adaptation), p. 12
questions.quote: multiplying the child’s weight (in kg) times 75

questions.subject: NP I
questions.situation: At the barangay health station, Nurse Joy assesses 2-year-old Migo, who weighs 12 kg and has had diarrhea for 3 days. He is restless and irritable, has sunken eyes, drinks eagerly, and his skin pinch goes back slowly. There is no blood in the stool and no general danger sign.
questions.stem: Migo vomits while drinking the ORS. What should Nurse Joy tell his mother?
options: Stop the ORS and give a soft drink instead
Wait 10 minutes, then continue more slowly
Give the ORS faster to replace the loss
questions.rationale: If the child vomits, wait 10 minutes, then continue giving ORS in small, frequent sips from a cup, more slowly.
explanations: Soft drinks are not appropriate rehydration fluids.
Correct: pause, then continue more slowly.
Faster intake makes vomiting more likely.
Stopping fluids worsens dehydration.
questions.source: WHO IMCI Chart Booklet (Afghanistan adaptation), p. 12
questions.quote: If the child vomits, wait 10 minutes. Then continue, but more slowly.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.situation: At the barangay health station, Nurse Joy assesses 2-year-old Migo, who weighs 12 kg and has had diarrhea for 3 days. He is restless and irritable, has sunken eyes, drinks eagerly, and his skin pinch goes back slowly. There is no blood in the stool and no general danger sign.
questions.stem: After 4 hours of Plan B, what should Nurse Joy do next?
options: Reassess Migo, reclassify, and choose Plan A, B, or C
Start IV fluids as routine follow-through
Repeat Plan B for 4 more hours automatically
questions.rationale: After 4 hours, the nurse reassesses and reclassifies the child's dehydration, chooses the plan that fits the new classification, and begins feeding in the clinic.
explanations: Correct: reassess and reclassify before choosing a plan.
Reassessment is required before discharge.
IV fluids are only for severe dehydration (Plan C).
The next plan depends on the reassessment.
questions.source: WHO IMCI Chart Booklet (Afghanistan adaptation), p. 12
questions.quote: Reassess the child and classify the child for dehydration.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: An 8-month-old with severe dehydration is started on IV Ringer's lactate under Plan C. How is the 100 mL/kg given?
options: 30 mL/kg in 30 minutes, then 70 mL/kg in 2½ hours
70 mL/kg in 1 hour, then 30 mL/kg in 5 hours
30 mL/kg in 1 hour, then 70 mL/kg in 5 hours
questions.rationale: For infants under 12 months, give 30 mL/kg in 1 hour, then 70 mL/kg in 5 hours. Children 12 months to 5 years get 30 mL/kg in 30 minutes, then 70 mL/kg in 2½ hours.
explanations: This schedule is for children 12 months up to 5 years.
The order of the volumes is reversed.
Too slow for severe dehydration.
Correct: the infant schedule under Plan C.
questions.source: WHO IMCI Chart Booklet (Afghanistan adaptation), p. 13
questions.quote: Give 100 ml/kg Ringer’s Lactate Solution (or, if not available, normal saline)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A 4-week-old infant has a respiratory rate of 64 breaths per minute on a repeat count. How does the nurse classify this using IMCI for the sick young infant?
questions.rationale: In a young infant (birth to 2 months), fast breathing of 60 or more per minute is a sign of POSSIBLE SERIOUS BACTERIAL INFECTION, which needs a first dose of IM antibiotics and urgent referral.
explanations: Local infection involves the umbilicus, skin, or eyes only.
Correct: 60 or more breaths per minute in a young infant.
This classification applies to older children without signs.
Sixty or more is fast breathing at this age.
questions.source: WHO IMCI Chart Booklet (Afghanistan adaptation), p. 22
questions.quote: Fast breathing (60 breaths per minute or more)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Under IMCI, a young infant's diarrhea is classified as SEVERE PERSISTENT DIARRHEA when it has lasted:
questions.rationale: Diarrhea lasting 14 days or more is persistent; in a young infant it is classified as severe persistent diarrhea and referred, after treating any dehydration.
explanations: Three days is acute diarrhea.
Seven days is still acute.
Correct: 14 days or more.
The threshold is 14 days.
questions.source: WHO IMCI Chart Booklet (Afghanistan adaptation), p. 23
questions.quote: Diarrhoea lasting 14 days or more

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: The community health nurse plans tuberculosis case-finding. Which group should be targeted as HIGH RISK?
options: Residents of a home for the aged
questions.rationale: Older adults, especially those in long-term care, are at high risk for TB. So are children 5 and under and people who are malnourished, immunosuppressed, or economically disadvantaged.
explanations: Correct: older adults in long-term care are high risk.
Healthy working adults are not a high-risk group.
Healthy adolescents are not a high-risk group.
Age and marital status alone are not risk factors.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 901)
questions.quote: Older clients, particularly those in long-term-care facilities, are at high risk for infection with TB.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A mother asks how long her child with chickenpox must be kept away from other children. What should the nurse say?
options: For 24 hours after the rash appears
Until all the vesicles have dried and crusted
Isolation is not needed once antipyretics are given
questions.rationale: Varicella is communicable from 1 to 2 days before the rash until the vesicles have crusted, about 6 days after the first crop. It spreads through vesicle fluid and respiratory secretions.
explanations: The child stays contagious after the fever resolves.
The child stays contagious for several more days.
Correct: contagious until all lesions crust.
Antipyretics do not affect contagiousness.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 601)
questions.quote: The communicable period is from 1 to 2 days before the onset of the rash to 6 days after the first crop of vesicles, when crusts have formed.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Community Health Nursing Process & Primary Health Care
questions.stem: During a women's health class in the barangay, the nurse discusses cervical cancer. Which is a risk factor?
options: Early age at first sexual intercourse
questions.rationale: Risk factors include HPV infection, multiple sexual partners (or a partner with multiple partners), smoking, and early first intercourse.
explanations: A single partner is not a risk factor.
Condoms reduce the risk of HPV transmission.
Not smoking lowers the risk.
Correct: early first intercourse is a risk factor.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 840)
questions.quote: Some risk factors for cervical cancer include having multiple sexual partners or a partner who had multiple sexual partners, smoking tobacco, early age of first intercourse, and HPV infection.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: At a community health screening, which client should the nurse prioritize for teaching on preventing respiratory disease?
options: A nonsmoker who works in an air-conditioned office
A smoker who works in a paint factory
A nonsmoker who jogs every morning
A former smoker who quit 20 years ago
questions.rationale: Smoking greatly raises respiratory risk, and exposure to chemicals, airborne toxins, dust, or fumes adds to it. The client with both risk factors is the priority.
explanations: This client has no major risk factor.
Correct: smoking plus occupational fumes.
This client has no identified risk factor.
This client's risk has decreased with years of not smoking.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 862)
questions.quote: Other risk factors include exposure to harmful chemicals, airborne toxins, and dust or fumes.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: The nurse helps a repeatedly abused woman recover from the physical and emotional effects of the abuse and prevent future abuse. Which level of prevention is this?
questions.rationale: Tertiary prevention is needed once a woman has been repeatedly abused. It focuses on overcoming the effects of the abuse and preventing it from happening again.
explanations: Correct: rehabilitation after repeated harm.
Primary prevention acts before any abuse occurs.
Secondary prevention is early detection and prompt treatment.
Primordial prevention addresses root social conditions before risk factors appear.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 886)
questions.quote: Tertiary prevention is necessary when a woman has been repeatedly abused.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: The duty not to inflict harm, and to prevent and remove harm, is the ethical principle of:
questions.rationale: Nonmaleficence is the duty not to inflict harm and to prevent and remove harm. Beneficence is doing good, veracity is truth-telling, and autonomy is self-determination.
explanations: Beneficence is the duty to do good.
Veracity is truth-telling.
Correct: the duty to do no harm.
Autonomy is the client's right to choose.
questions.source: Brunner & Suddarth's Medical-Surgical Nursing 16e Test Bank, Ch. 1 answer key
questions.quote: The duty not to inflict as well as prevent and remove harm is termed nonmaleficence.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A competent adult client refuses a procedure after a full explanation, but the physician tells the staff to proceed anyway. Which ethical principle is being violated?
questions.rationale: Autonomy is the right to make a choice free from external constraints. Overriding a competent client's informed refusal violates it.
explanations: Fidelity is keeping promises.
Correct: the client's informed choice is overridden.
Veracity is truth-telling.
Justice is the fair distribution of care.
questions.source: Brunner & Suddarth's Medical-Surgical Nursing 16e Test Bank, Ch. 1 answer key
questions.quote: The principle of autonomy specifies that individuals have the ability to make a choice free from external constraints.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which is an INTERDEPENDENT nursing action?
options: Assessing the apical pulse on admission
Teaching a client about discharge care
Giving mouth care to an unconscious client
Giving an IV fluid bolus as prescribed
questions.rationale: Interdependent actions carry out prescribed treatments and need a health care provider's order, such as IV fluids, pain medication, or wound irrigation. Assessment, teaching, and basic care are independent nursing actions.
explanations: Assessment is an independent nursing action.
Teaching is an independent nursing action.
Hygiene care is an independent nursing action.
Correct: IV fluids require a prescription.
questions.source: Brunner & Suddarth's Medical-Surgical Nursing 16e Test Bank, Ch. 1 answer key
questions.quote: Irrigating a wound, administering pain medication, and administering IV fluids are interdependent nursing actions and require a health care provider's order.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A physician tells a client, in front of other patients, that the nurse 'does not know anything.' The statement is false and harms the nurse's reputation. This is an example of:
questions.rationale: Defamation is a falsehood that injures a person's good name: spoken defamation is slander, and written defamation is libel. Assault is a threat of harm, and battery is unconsented touching.
explanations: Correct: spoken defamation.
Libel is written defamation.
Assault is putting someone in fear of harm.
Battery is touching without consent.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed. (PDF p. 604)
questions.quote: Defamation takes place when a falsehood is said (slander) or written (libel) about a person that results in injury to that person’s good name and reputation.
